disease_label_per_paper: Precursor B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia presenting as obstructive jaundice
presentation_summary: 44-year-old Hispanic man presented with weeks of right-upper-quadrant pain, jaundice, intermittent nausea and vomiting, weakness, poor appetite, clay-colored stools, and mild generalized itching.
Exam showed pallor, icteric sclerae, non-tender hepatomegaly, and normal vital signs.

Initial labs showed pancytopenia and obstructive-pattern cholestasis: hemoglobin 8.9 g/dL, WBC 3.6 x10^9/L, platelets 94 x10^9/L, total bilirubin 10 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 7 mg/dL, ALT 74 U/L, AST 52 U/L, ALP 293 U/L, GGT 327 U/L, LDH 319 U/L, and low reticulocyte production index.
Imaging did not show intra- or extra-hepatic bile duct dilatation; liver biopsy and marrow testing confirmed precursor B-cell ALL with hepatic lymphoblast infiltration and bile stasis.

quality_warnings: The cholestatic presentation is preserved as ordinary evidence and should not be removed because it mimics biliary disease.
Biopsy, IHC, marrow flow, cytogenetics, and CSF findings are confirmatory/context evidence with use_in_ranking:false.
